title: Neural Circuit Architectural Priors for Rat Locomotion
abstract: arXiv:2611.23364v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Animals generate behavior through continuous interactions between their neural circuits, bodies, and environment. Embodied simulations study these interactions by testing neural circuit models in biologically realistic settings. Recent efforts have simulated diverse animals, and emerging work on biologically grounded neural architectures has begun to integrate circuit connectivity and single-unit dynamics from experimental data into artificial neural networks, introducing stronger inductive biases and closer mechanistic alignment with biology. How can we develop embodied simulations that enable the study of increasingly complex bodies and neural circuits? In this work, we address the challenge through coordinated advances in the simulated body, neural architecture, and training infrastructure. translated_title: 面向大鼠运动的神经回路架构先验
translated_abstract: 动物通过神经回路、身体与环境之间的持续相互作用来产生行为。具身模拟通过在生物学逼真的环境中测试神经回路模型来研究这些相互作用。近期的研究已经模拟了多种多样的动物，而新兴的生物学基础神经架构研究已开始将实验数据中的回路连接方式与单神经元动力学整合进人工神经网络，从而引入更强的归纳偏置，并在机制层面更贴近生物学。我们如何开发出能够研究日益复杂的身体与神经回路的具身模拟？在本工作中，我们通过对模拟身体、神经架构和训练基础设施三方面的协同改进来应对这一挑战。我们提出了Rat v2，一个高效且灵活的生物力学大鼠身体模型，用于模拟大鼠行为。为了控制这一身体模型，我们开发了Rat NCAP，一种基于生物学
tldr: 该论文通过协同改进生物力学大鼠身体模型（Rat v2）、融合实验数据的神经回路架构先验（Rat NCAP）以及训练基础设施，构建了能够研究复杂身体与神经回路相互作用产生大鼠运动行为的具身模拟框架。
en_tdlr: This paper presents an embodied simulation framework that integrates an efficient biomechanical rat body (Rat v2), biologically grounded neural circuit architectural priors (Rat NCAP), and improved training infrastructure to study how complex bodies and neural circuits interact to generate rat locomotion.
